newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks again hit new closing high.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks again hit new closing high.

text.p: Swiss shares ended narrowly off their intra-day high, but were still able to post a second closing high in a row.
Foreign buying, a recovery in the U.S. dollar and Wall Street's overnight gains were the main reasons behind the rise, dealers said.
Also, several shares were in demand due to warrant issues.
But one dealer warned prices may come down given the current record levels.
"We may well see a consolidation in the next few sessions," he said.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended up 41.7 points, or 0.83 percent, to 5,084.2 points. An all-time high was reached at 5,086.8.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) climbed 25.39 points to end at 3,212.87, up 0.8 percent.
Among major banks, CS Group and SBC were reportedly pressured by switches into UBS, which soared 34 francs, or 2.4 percent, to 1,439 francs.
Novartis registered shares were seen profiting from news that the pharmaceutical company bought Merck's crop protection business for $910 million. The stock surged 26 francs to 2,009.
Roche also gained ground, climbing 175 francs to 12,905.
Among insurers, Winterthur was up three francs to 1,131.
The company is due to release 1996 results on Wednesday after the bourse close.

Shares of inspection firm Surveillance bounded 85 francs higher to 3,200 francs. The stocks were still drawing strength from Monday's news that a Swiss tax panel had confirmed SGS's position in a dispute over the tax treatment of share buybacks.
Recommendations by U.S. broker house also helped.
Alusuisse stocks were sought due to options-related buying, dealers said. They climbed 38 francs to 1,315.
Holderbank, Ciba, Ems, Clariant and Swiss Re were down.
